## OAMI Products

The engineers behind the OAMI technology have designed state-of-the-art products that are a world
first. These products are physical devices that works along with the latest AI technology which
impowers homeowners to take complete control over the electricity consumption in their homes for
little to no cost. These products could help homeowners to account for each and every kWh
electricity they consume. Depending on the utility provider, the consumer could not only save money
but could also be compensated by the utility for generating electricity using a privately owned
electricity generating device such as a grid-tied solar system.

These physical products and unqiue software can also help municipal and reseller utilities to
implement complicated tariff structures like Time-Of-Use, grid-tied solar systems and owner
self-generation. Not to mention the cost savings benefits to the utility company by using the
specialised communication network provided by these OAMI products.

There are a myriad of advantages by using these products, but the greatest advantage is that it is a
win-win for all parties. It helps utility providers to minimize loss and illegal consumption, and it
ensures that the end-user or homeowner is billed fairly.


#### In short these products are:


#### [The Utility Hub][22]

The Utilities Hub is a small box that can be installed on the Wi-Fi network of an electricity
consumer. The aim of the unit is to save electricity costs by making optimal use of the tariff
structure.

[Read More...][23]

#### [Meter Communication Modules][24]

These modules make communication to meters effortless and efficient, especially at large complexes,
where meter readers have difficulty gaining access or where meter readers are not available.

[Read More...][25]

#### [Voltage sensors][26]

Voltage sensors are wired or wireless components that can be attached to any number of meters,
switches or equipment. They constantly monitor, calculate and determine the voltage supply, and
provide enough information to ensure the user identify problems as soon as they occur.

## 旺玖科技

### 全球知名的 IC 設計領導廠商

旺玖科技為一家全球知名的 IC 設計領導廠商，專注於 USB
智慧型輸出入控制晶片、機電整合技術及智慧綠色能源解決方案。旺玖科技提供的晶片系統整合解決方案，包含
USB 介面橋接晶片、USB
儲存產品、無刷馬達控制器、霍爾原件感測器、智能電表及微機電感測器相關產品。旺玖科技成立於 1997 年 11
月，公司總部設於台灣，並於中國大陸、美國、日本、韓國等地區設有銷售服務據點。

# Innovative, nachhaltige

# für die Energiebranche

## Damit Sie zukunftssicher mit EFR steuern, messen und kommunizieren.

[Serviceprovider Netzsteuerung][57]
[Unsere Systemlösungen][58]
[Mehr über uns erfahren][59]

### Seit 30 Jahren vertrauen mehr als 350 Unternehmen und Kommunen unseren Systemlösungen.

## Unsere Systemlösungen für die Energiebranche

Die EFR-Systemlösungen umfassen alles Erforderliche für das Management und die
End-to-End-Kommunikation: Software, mehrere Kommunikationskanäle zur Auswahl und die passenden
Hardwarekomponenten.
Ziel ist die zuverlässige Umsetzung von Netzführungsaufgaben.

Da alle Komponenten des Systems aufeinander abgestimmt sind, lassen sich die EFR-System-Lösungen
auch bei umfassender Funktionalität einfach einführen und bedienen.

### Bereit für den Smart-Grid-Rollout?

Wir haben ein Vollservice-Angebot für das Einspeisemanagement nach § 9 EEG und das Steuern nach §
14a EnWG für Sie entwickelt.

[Unser Pilotsystem][60]

### Tarif- und Laststeuerung

Für die Tarif- und Laststeuerung bieten wir Lösungen mit dem EFR-Langwellen-Broadcastsystem, unsere
Hybridlösung oder die modulare Softwareplattform GMS.

[Unsere Tarif- und Laststeuerung][61]

### Redispatch 2.0 / Einspeisemanagement

Die faire Lösung, um Einspeiser erneuerbarer Energie ans Netz zu nehmen und Überlastungen zu
vermeiden. Intuitiv zu bedienen, sicher in der Anwendung. 

[Unser Redispatch 2.0 / Einspeisemanagement][62]

### Beleuchtungssteuerung

Unser auf Langwelle basierende Lösung zum Steuern der öffentlichen Beleuchtung – preiswert, schnell
und zuverlässig. 

[Unsere Beleuchtungssteuerung][63]

### M2M Mobilfunk

Die einfache Lösung zur Anbindung IP-basierter Endgeräte. Zum kleinen Tarif, aber mit einer
großartigen Netzverfügbarkeit.

# Smart Meters

## What is SmartMe?

SmartMe is an independent UK website explaining how electricity and gas smart meters work.

The site provides clear technical explanations of the UK smart meter system, including how smart
meters communicate, the differences between SMETS1 and SMETS2 meters, and how consumers can monitor
and understand their energy usage.

SmartMe was created by engineers with experience in smart meter technology and energy systems. The
goal of the site is to provide accurate, easy-to-understand information about smart meters, how they
operate, and how they affect households across the United Kingdom.

Topics covered on SmartMe include:
* How smart meters work
* SMETS1 vs SMETS2 meters
* Smart meter communications networks
* Home Area Networks and In-Home Displays
* The UK smart meter rollout
* Common smart meter questions and problems.

## The truth about Smart Meters - the good and the bad

[Simple diagram showing how meters and IHD connect.]

Energy supply companies have been installing smart meters for electricity and gas in homes across
Great Britain since 2012. By 2025, all residential and small businesses across England, Scotland and
Wales will be offered a smart meter by their energy supplier.

In Northern Ireland the Department for the Economy (DfE) has recommended an electricity smart meter
roll-out over six years starting in 2027. A gas roll-out won't be included as the benefits were not
sufficient.

A smart meter sends an electronic meter reading to your energy supplier, meaning:
* they won't need to take a manual meter reading - as the meters send back readings themselves
* you won't get estimated bills - as actual readings are available
* it'll be easier to switch energy suppliers - as the reading at changeover is readily available
* there should be less arguments - as the readings are reliable and not subject to disagreement.

You'll also get a digital display in your home, helping you to keep track of how much energy you're
using and how much it's costing.

You won't have to pay for your smart meter or digital display up front - the cost will be included
in everyone's energy bill over the next few years.

A smart meter won't change how you currently pay for your energy bill, e.g. monthly, or prepaid.
This will still be determined by the product and payment method you choose.

Smart Meters and their roll-out haven't been perfect and they've been the subject of negative
headlines. What do these headlines really mean?
* **Smart Meters don't work** - this headline has covered different problems over time, so let's
  break it down into the different reasons:
  * **Incorrect Bills** - When the Smart Meters fail to send in readings suppliers use estimates.
    This can go on for a while and can sometimes result in an unexpectedly large bill when a reading
    finally gets through.
    The meters are still recording accurately so customers just need to check their bill is not
    using estimates and send in a [manual reading][36] if necessary. If you do not want to check
    your bill just send in a meter reading every month as you would with a traditional meter.
  * **IHD not working** - Many customers call the In Home Device that usually sits on the worktop in
    their kitchen their “meter”. So, when that doesn't work they complain their meter is not
    working. Their meter is working and recording energy accurately but, frustratingly, they cannot

# Smart Meters

## What is SmartMe?

SmartMe is an independent UK website explaining how electricity and gas smart meters work.

The site provides clear technical explanations of the UK smart meter system, including how smart
meters communicate, the differences between SMETS1 and SMETS2 meters, and how consumers can monitor
and understand their energy usage.

SmartMe was created by engineers with experience in smart meter technology and energy systems. The
goal of the site is to provide accurate, easy-to-understand information about smart meters, how they
operate, and how they affect households across the United Kingdom.

Topics covered on SmartMe include:
* How smart meters work
* SMETS1 vs SMETS2 meters
* Smart meter communications networks
* Home Area Networks and In-Home Displays
* The UK smart meter rollout
* Common smart meter questions and problems.

## The truth about Smart Meters - the good and the bad

[Simple diagram showing how meters and IHD connect.]

Energy supply companies have been installing smart meters for electricity and gas in homes across
Great Britain since 2012. By 2025, all residential and small businesses across England, Scotland and
Wales will be offered a smart meter by their energy supplier.

In Northern Ireland the Department for the Economy (DfE) has recommended an electricity smart meter
roll-out over six years starting in 2027. A gas roll-out won't be included as the benefits were not
sufficient.

A smart meter sends an electronic meter reading to your energy supplier, meaning:
* they won't need to take a manual meter reading - as the meters send back readings themselves
* you won't get estimated bills - as actual readings are available
* it'll be easier to switch energy suppliers - as the reading at changeover is readily available
* there should be less arguments - as the readings are reliable and not subject to disagreement.

You'll also get a digital display in your home, helping you to keep track of how much energy you're
using and how much it's costing.

You won't have to pay for your smart meter or digital display up front - the cost will be included
in everyone's energy bill over the next few years.

A smart meter won't change how you currently pay for your energy bill, e.g. monthly, or prepaid.
This will still be determined by the product and payment method you choose.

Smart Meters and their roll-out haven't been perfect and they've been the subject of negative
headlines. What do these headlines really mean?
* **Smart Meters don't work** - this headline has covered different problems over time, so let's
  break it down into the different reasons:
  * **Incorrect Bills** - When the Smart Meters fail to send in readings suppliers use estimates.
    This can go on for a while and can sometimes result in an unexpectedly large bill when a reading
    finally gets through.
    The meters are still recording accurately so customers just need to check their bill is not
    using estimates and send in a [manual reading][36] if necessary. If you do not want to check
    your bill just send in a meter reading every month as you would with a traditional meter.
  * **IHD not working** - Many customers call the In Home Device that usually sits on the worktop in
    their kitchen their “meter”. So, when that doesn't work they complain their meter is not
    working. Their meter is working and recording energy accurately but, frustratingly, they cannot
    see that on the IHD. They have to go to their meter to [read][37] their consumption.
    Solutions to the IHD being too far away from the Comms Hub are being investigated by the [Alt
    HAN Co Ltd][38].
  * **No communications** - Communication with the meters is essential to set up tariffs and
    prepayment mode. Without communications your meter will operate as a traditional one rate meter,
    and you'll have to take your own readings. Understandably customers get very frustrated when
    their meters can't communicate and yet they have a good mobile signal and a good broadband
    connection. Progress to find alternative solutions for the [Wide Area Network (WAN)][39] have
    been slow which is again frustrating as the barriers to a solution are not technical but
    political.
  * **Stops working after changing supplier** - Older [SMETS 1][40] meters operated on many
    different management systems and could not always be supported when a customer changed supplier
    as the systems tended to be supplier specific. [SMETS 2][41] meters do not have this problem as
    a common system is used operated by the Data Communications Company (DCC).
* **North South Divide** - As the characteristics of the North and South of the country are
  different, a different communications system was setup for the two areas. Each system has pros and
  cons but sensibly a longer-range radio system was used in the North. However, customers in the
  North can get frustrated when they have a perfectly good mobile phone signal and the Long Range
  Radio signal to their meter is too weak for communication to work successfully. This has now been
  addressed as mobile 4G communications can be used in Scotland and the North of England from
  30^{th} May 2025.
  So, one could now argue that the North has better communications options than the South. See more
  information on our [SMETS 2][42] page.

Many people have questions about Smart Meters, this website tries to answer them honestly for
electricity and gas meters, thoroughly and without bias. This site does not deal with Smart water
meters as our team do not have expertise in that area.

## About Us & Why We are
## **The Best For Metering Solutions**

The company is a fully Nigerian Company and was registered in 2019 to carry on the business of
producing STS-compliant pre-paid and post-paid Smart Meters that can accurately measure and collect
power consumption data from consumers and transmit the data back to the Distribution Companies and
to the consumers as well.

Our Smart Meters easily integrate with smart home appliances to facilitate energy management for the
Energy Users.

Our Smart Meters support Two-way Communication which provides excellent benefits to the Energy
Distributors.

Hello Safer Technology Supporter,

through congress that echo these efforts:

that are FREE if you can help us distribute them to spanish speaking communities.

file it with the FCC and send separate copies to elected officials. (You may want to convert it to a
pdf.)**

City Council members; your State Senator; your State Assembly rep; your US Congressperson; CA US

signature)

Fill in your name, address, email, etc. (follow the prompts).

Note: Express filings do not separate paragraphs or preserve formatting.

Standard submission preferred when sending a letter.

it populates.

Follow prompts. When asked what type of filing, choose: “Comment” …red means *required.

Submit your letter as a Word doc or pdf attachment and include any other attachments that support
your letter.
